title: Boat home to Seattle and news of his brother's burial
summary: After eleven days at sea and a train to New York, his landlady told him to call his mother: his youngest brother had just been buried.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, from Japan, you didn't go to Australia or anything like that.
No, no, that was the end of the trip.
That was the end of the trip. You came home.
That's when our contract ran out. And we left Japan, and they put us on a boat to come back here. It taken us eleven days to get to Seattle, Washington. Eleven
days. Kind of a slow boat. But that was fast for that time(?).
It was eleven days to get to Seattle, and we stayed in Seattle overnight, and we got a train the next day, and we come back to New York.

The first thing greeting me when I got to New York, my landlady says, "Call your mother right away." So I did, to let her know I was back from overseas. She said, "Your brother was just buried yesterday." Boy, it hit me like a ton of bricks. Well, that was one of my brothers. That was my youngest brother.
Not the one that you could have run into in Guam.
No, no. He had made it back home; he was back. But that's about all of that trip.
